recent_posts.title: Links from the JCON talk 'Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API on Raspberry Pi'
recent_posts.summary: A companion resource page for a JCON 2026 talk about using the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API, finalized in Java 22, to modernize hardware interaction on the Raspberry Pi via the Pi4J library. The talk covers how FFM replaces complex JNI/JNA-based code, reduces dependencies, improves performance through less memory copying, and enables control of LEDs, buttons, LCD displays, and sensors. The page provides a curated list of links covering Project Panama, Jextract, the Vector API, Pi4J's FFM plugin, and live demo code.

recent_posts.title: Debugging BentoFX in MelodyMatrix with Creator Matt Coley: Scenic View, Layout Issues, and Honest AI Code Review
recent_posts.summary: A live debugging session with BentoFX creator Matt Coley, exploring layout issues in the MelodyMatrix JavaFX application. The session covers using Scenic View to inspect the JavaFX scene graph, how BentoFX's pruning behavior conflicted with manually written animation and width-tracking code, and an honest critique of AI-generated code (Claude and Copilot) that duplicated functionality already handled by the library. A potential bug in BentoFX's divider mode behavior was also discovered during the session.

recent_posts.title: Testing Lottie4J JavaFX Animations in GitHub Actions Without a Display: JavaFX 26 Headless to the Rescue
recent_posts.summary: JavaFX 26 introduced a headless glass platform that enables running JavaFX rendering tests in CI environments without a display. This post walks through how the Lottie4J project used this feature to enable a previously disabled GitHub Actions test that compares JavaFX animation output against JavaScript reference screenshots. The solution uses a Maven profile that upgrades JavaFX to version 26 and Java to 25 only for the test run, while keeping the library itself on Java 21/JavaFX 21. Key JVM flags needed are -Dglass.platform=headless and --enable-native-access=javafx.graphics. The approach eliminates the need for Xvfb or Docker display tricks, and enables pixel-level regression testing of Lottie animation rendering on every CI push.

recent_posts.title: MelodyMatrix V1.0.0 Released: Shipping a JavaFX App with jDeploy, GitHub Actions, and Auto-Update
recent_posts.summary: MelodyMatrix, a JavaFX MIDI practice app for musicians, has reached its official V1.0.0 release. The post and accompanying video walk through the full release process with jDeploy creator Steve Hannah, covering how jDeploy creates native installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux, bundles its own JVM, handles auto-updates on launch, and uses GitHub Releases as the distribution backend. Topics include GitHub Actions workflow configuration, git tagging best practices, version numbering, preventing simultaneous workflow runs, and customizing installer splash screens. jDeploy is free and requires no Maven Central or npm account — your GitHub repo serves as the distribution channel.

Posts span from 2013 to 2026 and include tutorials, hardware experiments, library releases, conference talk links, and monthly JavaFX link roundups.

recent_posts.title: Java Programming for Raspberry Pi
recent_posts.summary: A book titled 'Java Programming for Raspberry Pi' (2026 edition) is available as an ebook on Leanpub. It covers Java fundamentals, installation on Raspberry Pi, hardware control using Pi4J, JavaFX UIs, Spring web interfaces, message queues for Arduino communication, and JBang examples. The book targets both Java beginners and experienced developers looking to extend into IoT and electronics projects. Sources are freely available on GitHub, and the ebook is pay-as-you-wish starting at $9.99.

recent_posts.title: Validating Pi4J V4 on real hardware, catching bugs, and exploring the Ikalogic logic analyser
recent_posts.summary: Pi4J contributor Tom Aarts and Frank Delporte discuss hardware testing for Pi4J V4, including the design of a Smoke Test hardware setup for repeatable integration testing on real Raspberry Pi hardware. The session covers a live bug reproduction involving virtual thread pinning in the FFM plugin that caused only 4 of 8 button listeners to fire on a 4-core Raspberry Pi. It also features a first look at the Ikalogic SE254 logic analyser for visualising PWM and SPI signals, plus discussion of the upcoming Pi4J drivers library, example rework plans, and practical observations on AI-assisted coding with GitHub Copilot and Claude.

recent_posts.title: Lottie4J 1.2.0: dotLottie Support, Marker Playback, Cropping, and a Big Speed Boost
recent_posts.summary: Lottie4J 1.2.0 is released with several major additions. The headline feature is support for the .lottie container format (a ZIP-based format that bundles animations, images, and a manifest), loadable via two new API methods. The player gains marker-based playback via play(startMarker, endMarker), cropping support, and proper resizing. Performance is significantly improved through reduced rendering passes and metadata caching, with one animation jumping from 20–30 FPS to ~50 FPS. A new adaptive rendering toggle trades sharpness for speed. Core model improvements include merge/modifier shapes, blend modes, spatial bezier interpolation, and missing model fields. The library also upgrades to Jackson 3, which changes the group ID from com.fasterxml.jackson to tools.jackson. Debug tooling has been refactored and the automated visual comparison test now supports .lottie files.

top_posts.title: 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS on Raspberry Pi 4 with USB BOOT
top_posts.summary: A practical guide to setting up 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS on a Raspberry Pi 4 using USB boot instead of a microSD card. Covers the bootloader update process, writing the 64-bit beta OS image to three different storage types (microSD, USB flash drive, SSD), and benchmarks comparing read/write speeds across all three. The USB 3.0 flash drive emerges as the clear winner with real read speeds of 246 MB/s vs 46 MB/s for microSD, while the WD Black SSD had compatibility issues with USB 3 boot.
